But how exactly do we harness the power of thought? This book sets out to answer that question. When it was first published in 1937, the United States was in the midst of the longest and most severe economic depression in its history. Napoleon Hill hoped the power of thought could spread to every corner of society—helping those devastated by the Great Depression, the unemployed, and the bankrupt find the strength to rebuild and rise again. Over the decades, this book has inspired countless minds and generations. Before choosing to "opt out" of the hustle in the 21st century, why not give yourself another chance? Read and apply the 13 principles of success distilled by the “Father of Success Literature,” Napoleon Hill—drawn from 25 years of research and interviews with over 500 successful individuals. Try it for yourself: can the positive thoughts you project manifest into the abundant reality described by the hundreds of achievers in this timeless classic?

title: Islamic architecture in Iran : poststructural theory and the architectural history of Iranian mosques
author: Khaghani, Saeid
summary: "The architecture of the Islamic world is predominantly considered in terms of a dual division between "tradition" and "modernity" - a division which, Saeid Khaghani here argues, has shaped and limited the narrative applied to this architecture. Khaghani introduces and reconsiders the mosques of eighth- to fifteenth-century Iran in terms of poststructural theory and developments in historiography in order to develop a brand new dialectical framework. Using the examples of mosques such as the Friday Mosques in Isfahan and Yazd as well as the Imam mosque in Isfahan, Khaghani presents a new way of thinking about and discussing Islamic architecture, making this valuable reading for all interested in the study of the art, architecture, and material culture of the Islamic world."--Publisher
